title: Common-range wind timing contrasts were negative in England and uncertain in Scotland in 1993-2015
abstract: We tested whether a common wind range gave a common short-term moth catch link in two UK regions and two periods. We used 12,689 ECN trap nights in 1993-2015. A conditional Poisson model fitted separate wind curves on the trap night and seven days before and after. All three speeds were from 0.5 to 4 m/s. The trap-night 1-to-3 m/s log catch change minus the mean displaced change was -0.684 and -0.666 in England, with corrected intervals below zero. Scottish contrasts were +0.321 and +0.056, with intervals that included zero. English results survived six model checks and each site removal. Early Scottish site-only contrasts had opposite signs. A common speed range alone did not give four clear negative contrasts. Selected records, missing zero catches in later data, few year groups and weak Scottish support limit inference. This is a test of a weather-catch relation, not a causal climate, population or air pollution effect. Code, aggregate results, exact input hashes and a tested reproduction route are included. External record tables stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Finite wind timing contrasts for four samples. Each interval adjusts for four tests within one specification. Primary models limit all three wind dates to 0.5-4 m/s.
